title: Managed Resources, Sharing, And Settings Surfaces
objective: Move managed product metadata and settings-heavy workflows onto Server V2, including MCPs, skills, plugins, providers, router config, workspace shares, cloud signin, and import/export/share flows.

steps.name: Implement MCP CRUD services and routes
steps.description: Add Server V2 CRUD for MCP definitions stored in the DB instead of relying on direct config-file mutation in the app or Tauri.
successFactors: MCP definitions can be listed, created, updated, and removed through Server V2.
The server DB is the source of truth for managed MCP metadata.
The routes are typed and auth-aware.

steps.name: Implement workspace-to-MCP assignment flows
steps.description: Use the linking tables to attach MCP definitions to one or many workspaces and project the effective config for affected workspaces.
successFactors: Assignments are explicit and workspace-scoped.
Later workspace creation can attach existing MCPs cleanly.
Projection updates are triggered after assignment changes.

steps.name: Implement skill metadata CRUD
steps.description: Add DB-backed CRUD for skills metadata and body references so skills stop being modeled primarily as app-local file mutations.
successFactors: Skill metadata has stable server-owned records.
Skill source or ownership status is preserved.
The public routes are typed and deletable from legacy use later.

steps.name: Implement skill materialization and install/import flows
steps.description: Add the server-owned logic that installs, imports, or materializes skill files from managed records and trusted remote sources like Skill Hub when needed.
successFactors: Skill installation/import flows run through the server.
Managed versus imported skill provenance is retained.
Filesystem projection stays behind the server boundary.

steps.name: Implement workspace-to-skill assignment flows
steps.description: Use linking tables to attach skills to workspaces and update effective config or projected files accordingly.
successFactors: Skills can be attached to specific workspaces.
Assignments are reflected in projected workspace config.
The API makes no global-by-default assumption.

steps.name: Implement plugin CRUD
steps.description: Move plugin definition and enablement management into Server V2 so plugin config editing is no longer a direct local JSONC mutation in the app.
successFactors: Plugin metadata and config are server-owned.
Enable/disable behavior can be expressed without direct file edits in the UI.
Projection or materialization happens through the server.

steps.name: Implement workspace-to-plugin assignment flows
steps.description: Attach plugins to workspaces explicitly through linking tables and ensure effective config projection updates correctly.
successFactors: Plugin assignment is workspace-scoped.
Assignments update effective workspace config deterministically.
The linking model is consistent with other managed concepts.

steps.name: Implement provider config CRUD and assignment
steps.description: Add DB-backed provider config definitions, auth references, and workspace assignments so provider configuration stops being primarily app-local state or direct config edits.
successFactors: Provider configs have server-owned records.
Workspace attachments are explicit.
Later cloud sync or import flows can reuse the same model.

steps.name: Implement cloud signin persistence and validation
steps.description: Move cloud signin metadata behind the server, including base URL, auth/session metadata, selected org, and validation status, while keeping only transient UI pieces in the app.
successFactors: Durable cloud signin state is server-owned.
The server can validate or refresh cloud metadata when needed.
The app no longer treats cloud signin as only local preference state.

steps.name: Implement router identity services and routes
steps.description: Add Server V2 CRUD for router identities so messaging identity state becomes server-level state instead of app or orchestrator config mutation.
successFactors: Router identities are stored in the server DB.
Routes exist for listing and mutating identity metadata.
Identity changes can flow into router config materialization later in this phase.

steps.name: Implement router binding services and routes
steps.description: Add Server V2 CRUD for router bindings and target metadata so the server can decide whether router startup is required and what effective routing behavior should be.
successFactors: Router bindings are server-owned records.
Binding state can drive router enablement decisions.
Routes are typed and easy to validate.

steps.name: Materialize effective router config
steps.description: Turn router identities and bindings into the effective runtime config consumed by the supervised router process so router product behavior is fed by server-owned data.
successFactors: Router config is generated from server state rather than app-side file edits.
Config materialization can trigger router apply/reload behavior.
The implementation matches the server-owned router model from the architecture docs.

steps.name: Implement router product routes
steps.description: Add the main router health, status, apply, identity, binding, and outbound-send product routes under Server V2 so the UI stops talking to router-adjacent control surfaces directly.
successFactors: The server exposes router product behavior through its own API.
The UI does not need direct router requests for migrated flows.
Route behavior matches the runtime supervisor and config materialization model.

steps.name: Implement workspace share services and routes
steps.description: Add DB-backed workspace share records and routes for exposing or revoking local workspaces with workspace-scoped access keys.
successFactors: Share access is scoped per workspace.
Share status and audit metadata are persisted.
The server can expose, revoke, and inspect shares through typed routes.

steps.name: Implement portable export on Server V2
steps.description: Port the portable workspace export builder into Server V2 so bundle/export behavior becomes a server capability and can use server-owned config state directly.
successFactors: Export runs through Server V2.
The export model respects portable-file and secret-safety rules.
The output matches current product expectations where still needed.

steps.name: Implement portable import on Server V2
steps.description: Port the portable import flow into Server V2 so import and merge behavior update the DB, projected config, and managed files through one server-owned path.
successFactors: Import runs through Server V2.
Replace and merge semantics are explicit and tested.
Import triggers the correct projection and reload follow-up.

steps.name: Implement shared bundle publish and fetch
steps.description: Move bundle publish/fetch behavior to Server V2 so sharing and trusted bundle retrieval become server capabilities rather than app-side orchestration.
successFactors: Shared bundle publish/fetch flows are available through the main server.
Trusted-origin or publisher rules are enforced server-side.
The app can consume the server routes instead of building payloads locally for everything.

steps.name: Migrate settings and share UI surfaces
steps.description: Move the app's settings-heavy flows for MCPs, skills, plugins, providers, router, cloud signin, and sharing/import-export onto Server V2 for the covered areas.
successFactors: The covered settings surfaces talk to Server V2 instead of direct local config mutation.
Legacy fallbacks remain isolated for anything not yet migrated.
The app can render managed item state from the server DB-backed model.

steps.name: Add managed-resource integration tests
steps.description: Write tests for CRUD, workspace assignment, projection, router config, shares, import/export, and cloud signin so settings-heavy product behavior is guarded before final cutover.
successFactors: Managed-resource route families have automated coverage.
Workspace assignment and projection behavior are asserted.
Import/export and share safety rules are exercised.

steps.name: Record cross-phase learnings for settings migration
steps.description: Capture any data-model, projection, or UI-migration learnings that later orchestrator-collapse or cutover work will need, and add them to the appropriate learnings files.
successFactors: Important settings migration lessons are not trapped inside one phase.
Later phases can see what temporary compatibility code still exists.
Phase 8 leaves settings surfaces much closer to the thin-client target.
